title: Progress, Stretch, X-Heights, Pre-Toggles & Real Controls
description: Animation.overallProgress, width: stretch, font-size-adjust, beforetoggle, and form-associated custom elements.

drops.title: Progress, In One Number
drops.description: Six animations with six durations and iteration counts, all read and seeked on the same 0→1 scale.
drops.concept: Every animation used to report its position in its own units — milliseconds against a duration you had to remember, or a per-iteration progress that reset three times on the way through. Animation.overallProgress is one number, 0 to 1, across all iterations and whatever the timeline. This drop runs six performers with different durations, iteration counts, easings and directions, prints each one's progress beside its raw currentTime, plots overallProgress against getComputedTiming().progress so the sawtooth is visible, and hangs one master scrubber off all six.
drops.source: DavMila — the animation.progress explainer behind the shipped property

interaction.mouse: Drag Master to seek all six to the same fraction of their own lives; drag seek to scrub the plotted animation
interaction.click: Play or hold the whole troupe; change the playback rate
interaction.touch: Same sliders, full width on a phone

drops.title: Fill the Box, Margins Included
drops.description: width: stretch sizes a box to what is left after its own margins — the thing width: 100% never did.
drops.concept: width: 100% has always meant 100% of the parent, with your margins added on top, which is why a margined child overflows its container by exactly twice the margin. The stretch keyword — the standard spelling of -webkit-fill-available — means fill what is actually available. Three boxes sit side by side under one margin slider, the overflow is measured in pixels rather than asserted, and the same trick is shown on the block axis and in a real action bar.

interaction.mouse: Drag Margin and watch one of the three boxes leave its dashed parent; drag Box to reflow the grid
interaction.click: Flip the width switch to turn the stretch column back into 100% in place
interaction.touch: Sliders and switch work the same; the grid collapses to one column

drops.title: Same Size, Different Size
drops.description: Five families at one identical font-size, looking nothing alike — until font-size-adjust pins the x-height.
drops.concept: What the eye reads as type size is the x-height, and every family takes a different share of the em for it. font-size-adjust gives the browser a target ratio and lets it re-solve the used font size to hit it. Because the adjusted size is a used value that getComputedStyle never reports, this drop measures it: paired probe strings, one inheriting the adjustment and one pinned to none, give the exact scale factor. The x-height rules are drawn from that measurement and snap into a row, and a headline swapping families every two seconds shows the layout shift the property removes.
drops.source: web.dev — “CSS font-size-adjust is now in Baseline”

interaction.mouse: Drag Aspect to set the target ratio by hand, or Size to move the declared size
interaction.click: Switch between none, match and custom; turn on the measured x-height rules
interaction.touch: Cards stack to one column, controls move inline above the stages

drops.title: The Moment Before It Opens
drops.description: beforetoggle fires while the panel is still display:none — early enough to aim it, early enough to refuse.
drops.concept: The toggle event tells you a panel opened; beforetoggle tells you one is about to, before a pixel is committed. That is the only frame in which you can read event.source, measure the button that summoned the panel and set its position and transform-origin without a flash of wrongly-placed UI. It is also cancelable on the way open but not on the way closed, so a page can refuse an opening and can never trap you inside one. A live log prints oldState→newState and cancelable for every event, including the ones it blocks.

interaction.mouse: Open the shared sheet from any of four buttons and watch it grow out of the right one
interaction.click: Flip the guard to refuse, then try the guarded sheet; open accordion panes and watch siblings close
interaction.touch: Every trigger is tap-sized; the log panel moves inline

drops.title: A Control the Form Believes In
drops.description: Three custom elements, no input between them, all showing up in FormData and blocking submission.
drops.concept: A web component next to a hidden input is not a form control; it is a decoration with a chaperone. static formAssociated = true plus attachInternals() makes it the real thing: setFormValue() puts it in the submission, setValidity() lets it block one with the browser's own message, and formResetCallback() makes form.reset() reach inside it. A star rating, a swatch picker and a two-handle range sit in one form — and the range shows the part that finally retires the hidden-input pair, because setFormValue() accepts a whole FormData and contributes two named entries from one element.

interaction.mouse: Pick stars, a swatch and a budget range; the panel re-reads FormData on every change
interaction.click: Submit to see the serialised body, Reset to watch formResetCallback clear each component
interaction.touch: All three controls are tap and drag friendly
